newsitem.title: JAPAN: HANDBALL-CROATIA OFF TO GOOD START IN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: HANDBALL-CROATIA OFF TO GOOD START IN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Olympic champions Croatia, powered by members of last summer's gold medal-winning squad, cruised to a 26-17 victory over Morocco on Monday to move to the top of Group D in the preliminaries of the men's handball world championship.
Croatia are undefeated with two wins and lead the group with Russia, who beat China 34-15 in this southwestern Japanese city.
Meanwhile, Yugoslavia took over the lead in Group A with a 29-21 win over Lithuania while Algeria edged Saudi Arabia 19-14.
Croatia, runners-up in the 1995 world championships, were helped by four goals each from Olympic team members Goran Perkovac, Nenad Kljaic, Patrik Cavar and Slavko Goluza.

Edouard Kokcharov netted nine goals and Denis Krivochlykov slammed in another eight as Russia, the 1993 world champions, scored an easy win over China, making their first appearance in the world championships.
Aleksandr Knezevic notched eight goals for Yugoslavia and Dragan Skrbic added six to counter the nine goals from Lithuania's Gediminas Bucys.
Redouane Saidi broke open a 6-3 game at halftime with five goals as African champions Algeria defeated tournament newcomers Saudi Arabia.
The preliminaries, being contested by 24 teams divided into four groups, continue until next Sunday.
The top four finishers in each group will advance to the final rounds starting next week.
